anchors: Pin each decision with a test that fails when the decision is reverted
decision: A jig records each choice a later editor could undo in a Decisions block in its module docstring, every entry pinned by a test that fails when the decision is reverted, and the block is read before a matcher, rule or threshold changes.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: hooks, jigs and scripts keep their reason in a Decisions block in the module docstring plus a regression test that goes red when the decision is reverted; no new file and no new gate for code

reopen_if: A jig decision is undone although its docstring entry and pinning test both carried it, or editors keep missing the block.
why: Jig rules were changed forward and back because the reason sat in a commit or a changelog the next editor never reads; the module and its tests are what that editor opens.

decision: Rejected: a decisions.jsonl ledger for hooks and jigs.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: skills get the ledger, code keeps its reason in the module docstring and a regression test; no new file and no new gate for code

reopen_if: a reverted code decision is found whose docstring and tests both carried it and it was still undone
why: code already carries its reason in the module docstring and its behaviour in a regression test; a second record would drift from both

decision: Not adopted: documenting where ci_wait's CI_RC= line lands when ci_wait runs as a backgrounded Bash call.
reopen_if: ci_wait.py starts printing a CI_RC= line or another fixed verdict line whose location a caller has to know.
why: Refuted: ci_wait.py prints no CI_RC= line (its verdict goes to stdout on success, to stderr otherwise). The line that went missing was the caller's own echo, written outside the redirect.

decision: Not adopted: rewording gate.py's --help line on --name, reported as contradicting the parser's refusal '--name must be written AFTER the --gate it labels'.
reopen_if: gate.py's help and its parser come to disagree on where --name goes, or the same line is misread again.
why: No contradiction: the help says a --name labels the --gate written before it, which is the rule the parser enforces. The report misread the help.

anchors: since `--ref` resolves in that `--repo` directory, else in the current directory's repo
decision: ci_wait --ref resolves in the --repo directory when --repo names a local checkout, else (no --repo, or OWNER/NAME) in the current repo; the skill says so in the ci_wait row and in the no-runs checklist.

evidence.text: tests/test_ci_wait.py::TestRefOnTheCommandLine::test_a_ref_is_resolved_inside_a_directory_repo_not_the_cwd fails on the pre-fix script and passes after; opus and haiku probes on the pre-edit text answered the cwd's HEAD, on the new text the worktree's HEAD, quoting it.

reopen_if: ci_wait stops resolving --ref in a --repo directory, or starts resolving it for an OWNER/NAME --repo some other way.
why: Run from the main checkout with --repo naming a linked worktree, --ref HEAD resolved in the cwd and reported the main checkout's verdict as the worktree's, a green for the wrong sha. The tool now resolves in the --repo directory, and text saying 'the current repo' would steer a reader to cd needlessly or to distrust a correct run.

anchors: then appended to `--log` after the gate commands' output
decision: gate.py appends its [PASS]/[FAIL] lines and the closing verdict to --log after the gate output, and opens each run in the log with cwd: and repo: lines; the gate row says so and tells a reader of a reused log to read the LAST verdict.

evidence.text: tests/test_gate.py::TestTheLogCarriesTheVerdictAndWhereItRan (8 tests) failed on the pre-fix gate.py and pass after; opus and haiku quote-back on the new row answered both questions with the governing sentence.

reopen_if: gate.py stops writing the verdict or the cwd/repo header into --log.
why: The old text said the verdict was printed only on stdout, never into --log, and agents still polled the log for ALL GATES PASSED and read its silence as a gate still running; several sessions gating the same command could not tell whose log was whose. Writing the verdict into the log removes the trap instead of documenting it.

anchors: whose git remotes all name a repository other than that `--repo`
decision: ci_wait refuses --ref with an OWNER/NAME --repo when the cwd has remotes and none names that repository, and --min-attempt N holds a run whose attempt is below N as still waiting; the ci_wait row says both.

evidence.text: tests/test_ci_wait.py TestRefAgainstAnOwnerNameRepo, TestNamesRepository, TestMinAttempt fail on the pre-fix script and pass after; opus quote-back answered both cases from the row, haiku's ambiguity about 'another repository' was closed by naming the --repo.

reopen_if: ci_wait drops the remote check or --min-attempt, or the check starts refusing a cwd with no remotes.
why: A --ref resolved in one checkout and polled against another repository ends no-runs after the grace period with nothing pointing at the cause; after gh run rerun the listing can still show the old attempt green, so the wait returned that stale success on its first poll.

anchors: `--test` takes ONE node id and repeats
decision: mutation_arm's --test takes one node id and repeats, a battery tests entry likewise; a value holding several paths or a pytest option is refused before anything is written, pytest exits 4 and 5 are reported as that and never as a red baseline, and --log-dir never overwrites an earlier log.

evidence.text: 17 new tests in tests/test_mutation_arm.py failed on the pre-fix script and pass after; opus and haiku quote-back answered the five questions from the row and the reference.

reopen_if: mutation_arm accepts a space-separated value again, or --log-dir starts reusing names.
why: A single string of paths and options made the baseline exit 4 and the tool reported a red baseline; a shared --log-dir silently overwrote earlier runs' logs; a module with slow tests ran a battery past the command limit.

anchors: Apply both to a new jig as a whole, and on an edit to an existing jig to the code the edit touches
decision: Writing or editing a jig loads coding-python-data-architecture and coding-python-performance-review: a new jig as a whole, an edit to an existing jig for the code the edit touches; a bash launcher follows the two bash skills instead.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-16: Python jigs and tools are written with the data architecture and performance skills

reopen_if: One of the two skills is renamed or merged, or the user narrows or widens the scope (for example to every script a change sits beside).
why: A jig is Python code that parses, scans and loops over caller-sized input, and the section said nothing about its data shapes or its cost; the two skills hold those rules, so the section points at them instead of restating them.

anchors: A poll line names only the jobs failed BY THAT POLL, so never quote one as the push's failed cells
decision: A failed ci_wait reads every job of every run once more and prints them above the verdict line (data.jobs in JSON); the ci_wait row tells the reader to take the failed cells from that block, never from a poll line, and that the verdict line stays last and unchanged.

evidence.text: tests/test_ci_wait.py TestAFailedWaitNamesEveryJob and TestFormatRunJobs fail on the pre-fix script and pass after; opus and haiku probes on the pre-edit row answered NONE for where the full failed list is, on the new row both quoted the poll-line sentence.

reopen_if: ci_wait stops printing the closing job block on a failed wait, or the verdict line stops being the last line a caller reads.
why: A poll line names only the jobs failed by that poll and the verdict line names runs, so a reader quoted one poll's failed macOS cell as the push's whole failure while the windows cell was still running, and windows failed too, which cost a second release.

anchors: A spent API rate limit is not weather: after each failed call the tool reads `gh api rate_limit`
decision: After a failed gh call ci_wait reads gh api rate_limit; core remaining 0 ends the wait at once as rate-limited, exit 2, naming the reset in local time and UTC, while an unreadable quota or one with requests left keeps the retry; the ci_wait row says so.

evidence.text: tests/test_ci_wait.py TestASpentRateLimitEndsTheWait: on the pre-fix script the exhausted case made 11 run listings, after the fix 1; opus and haiku probes on the pre-edit row read the 403 as retried, on the new row both quoted the rate-limited sentence.

reopen_if: ci_wait stops reading the quota after a failed call, or GitHub starts counting the rate_limit endpoint against the limit.
why: A 403 API rate limit exceeded was retried for the whole error grace, about ten more calls against a limit every session on the account shares, and still ended as error.
